chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman al-Asam from Mis'ma ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) did not accept the testimony of the one who had already performed Hajj.

key_terms.سَابِقِ الْحَاجِّ: The one who has performed Hajj / The pilgrim

ai.seo_question: Why was the testimony of a pilgrim not accepted during Hajj according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) is recorded as not accepting the testimony of a *sābiq al-ḥājj* (one who has performed Hajj but not yet returned or completed all rites), a ruling that highlights the precision of Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of witnesses based on their ritual state. This specific exclusion underscores the principle that legal capacity can be temporarily suspended by incomplete religious obligations, ensuring the integrity of judicial testimony. The ruling reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the continuity of ritual purity and completion of duties as prerequisites for full legal standing.
